summary: Jun Villanueva is a 25-year-old barista who has worked the espresso bar at Heron & Grind on Calle Ortega for three years. At the start of the horizon he lives in his mother Tess's house off Vinca Avenue and is trying to turn his family's pork-and-shrimp lumpia into a real business, Lola's Roll, with his best friend Paolo. He is charming behind the counter, trains coworkers on latte art and can sell anything to anyone, but receipts, permits and tax forms make him freeze. In late August he still needs a cottage food permit, steady commissary time at Joan Whitaker's Ruel Road kitchen and a vendor slot at Rick Dominguez's Delgado Park market. He wants Lola's Roll to be bigger than a side gig and to prove to his mother that it is a better path than nursing school. Pressing on him are the cost of kitchen hours, Paolo skipping early prep, and a savings account that drops every time he buys wrappers in bulk. By November he is hoping for a farmers market slot and enough holiday orders to cut his cafe hours.

impressions.statement: Charms his way through people problems but stalls for days on anything with a form or a number in it.

evidence.description: Asks the assistant to just tell him which box to check on the permit form, then admits it's been open in a tab for two weeks
Pastes a photo-transcribed pile of receipts and asks if he can just 'guess' the September ingredient total
After the county email says lumpia isn't cottage food, drafts a friendly message to Rick within minutes but leaves the health permit packet unopened until the weekend
Wants help writing a cheerful preorder post but says he'll 'do the tax part later' when asked about collecting sales tax

impressions.statement: Measures his worth through his mother's approval of the food, even while arguing against her plans for him.

evidence.description: Rewrites the lumpia filling ratio after Tess calls the batch 'too much onion,' even though it sold out
Asks for help wording a price-increase sign and worries more about what Tess will say than customers
Moving into the sublet, asks how to explain to Tess that he's not quitting coffee for nursing, just leaving home
Shares a photo caption crediting Tess's recipe and asks if 'Lola-approved, Mom-tested' sounds cheesy
Mentions Tess came to the market stall and said nothing about the wrappers, which he reads as high praise

impressions.statement: Leans on Linh's organized brain and feels a little sheepish about how much.

evidence.description: Asks the assistant to calculate cost per lumpia 'so I don't have to bug my coworker again'
After Linh builds the spreadsheet, asks for a thank-you gift idea that isn't coffee
Wants a formula fixed in the sales tab but says not to change her color coding
Asks how to offer Linh paid help on market Sundays without making it weird at work

impressions.statement: Covers for Paolo's flakiness long past the point it costs him, until it finally tips him into being direct.

evidence.description: Asks for a prep plan he can run solo 'in case Paolo's running late again'
Drafts a group text to Paolo, then softens it three times into a joke
Rolls 200 lumpia alone at the commissary and asks for hand-stretch tips at midnight
Asks for help writing a clear proposal changing the profit split, and keeps the firm version
Sends Paolo a set call time for market setup and doesn't apologize for it

impressions.changed_to: Sets clear expectations with Paolo instead of quietly absorbing the extra work.
